text:
acme_idp_admin: Hi, we rotated our IdP signing cert this morning and now users are getting a SAML login failure when redirecting back to Redwood. Error in our logs is `Signature verification failed`. Can you help?

amanda_support: sorry you're hitting this — can you paste the error you see on the SP (Redwood) side or a screenshot of the SAMLResponse error? also which app/entityID are you using?

acme_idp_admin: here's the SP-initiated redirect error we captured from the browser console: `POST https://app.redwood-inference.com/saml/acs 400 Bad Request` and the IdP logs show `Assertion signature validation failed`. Our entityID is `https://sso.acme-corp.com/metadata` and ACS set in app is `https://app.redwood-inference.com/saml/acs` (no trailing slash).

amanda_support: thanks. quick checklist we usually run: 1) confirm IdP metadata uploaded to console matches the cert currently served; 2) check for trailing slash mismatch on ACS; 3) ensure the KeyDescriptor order isn't breaking simple parsers after rotation; 4) verify SAMLResponse contains the expected issuer/entityID.

omar_infra: can you export the IdP metadata XML you uploaded and paste the `<KeyDescriptor use=\"signing\">` section (or the cert fingerprint)? also did you replace the cert or add a new `<KeyDescriptor>` alongside the old one?

acme_idp_admin: we replaced the cert entry — here is the snippet (sanitized):

```
<KeyDescriptor use="signing">
  <KeyInfo>
    <X509Data>
      <X509Certificate>MIIC...NEWCERT...Q==</X509Certificate>
    </X509Data>
  </KeyInfo>
</KeyDescriptor>
```

acme_idp_admin: and when i run `openssl x509 -in newcert.pem -noout -fingerprint -sha1` I get `SHA1 Fingerprint=AA:BB:CC:11:22:33:44:55:66:77:88:99:AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF:00:11`

jess_sre: two quick things we've seen cause this exact symptom: 1) ACS URL in the SP config includes a trailing slash (or missing it) — the assertion's Recipient/AssertionConsumerServiceURL must match exactly; 2) certs in the IdP metadata sometimes get canonicalized differently (line breaks/whitespace) and some SP parsers fail to parse the new cert if KeyDescriptor ordering changed.

amanda_support: can you grab the raw SAMLResponse (base64) from the browser network tab and paste it here (or DM if sensitive)? we can decode and check Issuer/Recipient and signature reference. if you prefer, run locally: `echo '<base64>' | base64 -d | xmllint --format -`

acme_idp_admin: pasted the base64 in DM to @amanda_support. decoded snippet shows:
```
<saml:Assertion>
  <saml:Issuer>https://sso.acme-corp.com/metadata</saml:Issuer>
  <saml:Subject>
    <saml:SubjectConfirmation>
      <saml:SubjectConfirmationData Recipient="https://app.redwood-inference.com/saml/acs" />
    </saml:SubjectConfirmation>
  </saml:Subject>
</saml:Assertion>
<ds:Signature>
  ...signature block...
</ds:Signature>
```

amanda_support: issuer and recipient look correct. can you check our SP logs for more detail? @jess_sre @omar_infra any chance the SP is still using a cached old cert or mismatched metadata? we do accept multiple KeyDescriptor entries but signature verification will fail if fingerprint mismatch.

omar_infra: checking the SP logs now. grabbing the auth debug trace...

omar_infra: log: `SAML: signature validation failed: X509CannotDecode` followed by `Unable to parse certificate: ASN1 error` — looks like the SP parser hits an ASN.1 decode error when trying to load the cert blob from metadata. that would explain `Signature verification failed`.

amanda_support: that points to malformed certificate blob in the metadata upload. sometimes copying from HTML or PDF can introduce hidden characters. can you re-download the metadata XML straight from the IdP endpoint and re-upload it to the Redwood console? the URL should be something like `https://sso.acme-corp.com/metadata.xml`.

acme_idp_admin: we pulled the metadata from our IdP admin UI — maybe there was a newline issue. i just downloaded the raw XML and re-uploaded to Redwood console. also confirmed the certificate block matches the openssl output.

saml-validator-bot: Automated check: metadata fetch OK, certificate base64 decodes to a valid X509 (subject CN=ACME IdP), SHA1 fingerprint AA:BB:CC:11:22:33:44:55:66:77:88:99:AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF:00:11. No whitespace anomalies detected.

acme_idp_admin: after re-upload users still see failure. same browser POST 400.

jess_sre: odd. can you confirm the Assertion's Signature `<SignedInfo><Reference URI>` matches the Assertion ID (no stray whitespace) and that the signature uses the same cert (fingerprint) as in metadata? also check if you have an intermediate cert required in chain — we only validate the signing cert itself but some IdPs sign with a subordinate cert and include chain entries.

amanda_support: also confirm your IdP isn't signing the response with an old key from the previous cert — sometimes IdP clusters have staggered key activation and send mixed certs briefly after rotation. that would show as a fingerprint mismatch in our logs.

acme_idp_admin: good catch — our auth logs show the Response is signed with fingerprint `AA:BB:CC:11:22:33:44:55:66:77:88:99:AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF:00:11` (the new one) but the Assertion is signed with `FF:EE:DD:CC:BB:AA:99:88:77:66:55:44:33:22:11:00:FF:EE:DD:CC` (old). we must have a rolling key config.

amanda_support: that's the smoking gun — our SP signature verification expects the cert in metadata to match the signature on the signed element. if your IdP sometimes signs Assertion with old key, we need both certs present in metadata (both KeyDescriptor entries). please add the old cert back into the metadata along with the new one or ensure cluster switches fully to the new key.

acme_idp_admin: would adding both certs look like this?
```
<KeyDescriptor use="signing">...OLDCERT...</KeyDescriptor>
<KeyDescriptor use="signing">...NEWCERT...</KeyDescriptor>
```

amanda_support: yes, exactly. order doesn't matter for validation but having both ensures signature verification succeeds during rotation windows. after you add both, re-upload and let us know — we can re-run a login.

acme_idp_admin: re-uploaded metadata with both keys. triggered a new login, user got in! :tada:

amanda_support: awesome. leaving a couple follow-ups: 1) try to schedule cert rotations during low traffic and keep dual-key metadata for N hours while all IdP nodes pick up new key; 2) if you need automation, we can add a pre-rotation check doc for your team. i'll create a small KB entry.

jess_sre: adding runbook items: `openssl x509 -in cert.pem -noout -fingerprint -sha1` to verify, `echo '<base64>' | base64 -d | xmllint --format -` to inspect SAMLResponse, and fetch metadata with `curl -sL https://sso.acme-corp.com/metadata.xml | xmllint --format -`. will paste runbook in #docs later.

amanda_support: closing loop — please reopen if anything else pops up. thanks for working through it so quickly. :thumbsup:
